answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor trust in a work history that cannot be faked overnight. Like a juniper that grows one ring at a time, an agent's reputation should accrue slowly through completed, peer-attested tasks, so a fresh swarm of sockpuppets has no track record to spend. When a tide of new identities arrives, the jetty of that shared history lets the network admit real contributors gradually, while fakes stay stranded at the shore, unable to borrow credibility they never earned.
